.github/workflows/release.yml
name: Create GitHub Release

# Tagging is the only manual release step. Pushing a "v*" tag creates the
# GitHub Release, then dispatches npm-publish.yml explicitly: releases
# created with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `on: release`, so event chaining
# alone silently skips npm publishing (#1187). workflow_dispatch is the
# documented GITHUB_TOKEN exception.
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Derive version from tag
        id: version
        run: |
          TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          echo "tag=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=${TAG#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Verify release commit is on main
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main; then
            echo "::error::Release tag commit $(git rev-parse HEAD) is not an ancestor of origin/main. Releasing is only allowed from the main branch."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Root cause of #1033: fail the release if root `dev-loops` ships an
      # `@dev-loops/core` dependency whose major.minor differs from the version
      # being released (e.g. dev-loops@0.6.2 carrying @dev-loops/core@^0.2.6).
      # node-builtins-only, so it runs without `npm ci`.
      - name: Assert @dev-loops/core dependency is in lockstep with the release
        run: |
          node scripts/release/assert-core-dependency-version.mjs \
            --release-version "${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"

      - name: Skip if release already exists (idempotent)
        id: exists
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if gh release view "${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::notice::Release ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }} already exists; nothing to do."
            echo "exists=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "exists=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Extract release notes from CHANGELOG.md (fail closed)
        if: steps.exists.outputs.exists == 'false'
        run: |
          node scripts/release/extract-changelog-section.mjs \
            --version "${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}" \
            > release-notes.md

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        if: steps.exists.outputs.exists == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release create "${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}" \
            --title "${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}" \
            --notes-file release-notes.md \
            --latest \
            --verify-tag

      # Not gated on `exists`: re-running after a failed dispatch/publish must
      # retry. npm-publish.yml itself skips versions already on the registry.
      - name: Dispatch npm publish for the release tag
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh workflow run npm-publish.yml --ref "${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}"

## Problem

`npm-publish.yml` triggers on `release: published`, but `release.yml` creates releases using `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub Actions suppresses workflow triggers for events created by `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so npm publishing has silently not happened since v0.6.0 — 0.6.2, 0.7.0, and 0.7.1 were tagged and released on GitHub but never published to npm.

v0.7.1 was unblocked manually by draft-toggling the release with a user token (real-user `published` events do chain).

## Fix

Use the documented exception: `workflow_dispatch` triggered via `GITHUB_TOKEN` *does* start workflows.

- `npm-publish.yml`: add `workflow_dispatch:` to `on:` (dispatch with `--ref <tag>` checks out the tag; version derives from the checked-out package.json as today).
- `release.yml`: grant `actions: write` and, after creating the release, run `gh workflow run npm-publish.yml --ref "$TAG"`.

Manual UI-published releases keep working via the existing `release: published` trigger.

## Acceptance criteria

- Creating a release via release.yml results in an npm-publish run for the same tag.
- Existing `release: published` path unchanged.
- Idempotent re-runs (revised during draft-gate review): the dispatch step is not gated on the release already existing, and each publish step skips with a visible `::notice::` when that package@version is already on the registry — a re-run after a partial failure (e.g. core published, root failed) must retry the missing package and end green, not fail on the one that already made it.
